findings.label: contradictory probing ownership
findings.summary: The probing contract gives the root mutually incompatible ownership of paid and harness probes.
findings.detail: The probing mechanics say “paid or harness probes stay with the root,” while the later “Root stays idle” rule says the root delegates every research, paid, and harness probe and explicitly says it replaces that handoff. A Developer cannot implement both, and either choice can violate the live-flow proof. Remove the obsolete stay-with-root rule and retain one exact ownership rule, with its corresponding test/proof.

findings.label: live target contract underspecified
findings.summary: The paid target is named, but its fixture route, profiles, login, preflights, and complete budget are not specified in these scenarios.
findings.detail: Both selected live proofs rely on live-shaping-quality, yet the contract only says it is a real Codex target and mentions 600 s case/180 s auditor limits. It does not identify the fixture route, selected profiles, login/setup, preflight/readiness checks, or the target-level time budget. This leaves the paid observation unguarded and permits a wrong fixture or unready provider run to count as proof. Add one exact live-target configuration and preflight contract (or cite the authoritative fixture scenario) and assert those fields offline.
